GENERAL UPDATE

In this post, I wanted to tell you all what I've been up to for a month of apparent silence. The following are some things I now know how to pull off that I didn't quite know how to do before. Some of these are used in the one-shot i’m making for @gabara while the others show up in a mystery project that I don't wish to reveal yet. some got prototyped in both, in slightly different ways.

Also, COSMOS PURITY has a little piece of news at the end of this post as well.

-random generation and management of map attributes/objects, plus AI generated stories/events. Semi-defined map generation, not totally-free map generation. IE I can now change a set population of map tiles, but, i’m not yet anywhere near generating a minecraft map. If its a system where the parts don’t ever escape their limited and defined boundaries, I can probably be its master.

-several rough NPC functions.

-timed environment functions such as seasons, and day/night cycles

-broader testing in regards to handling and moving data between differing game scenes. While the unity engine lets you mark certain objects as do-not-delete between scenes, highly complex problems start happening as soon as duplicate objects start becoming a factor. IE scene 1 has object A, which is loaded then into scene 2, then back to scene 1, leaving 2 identical instances of object A. obviously, this creates a few errors. Many of these tests were figuring out how to prevent this difficulty

-finer control over audio transitions, especially between loading up new scenes. Playing multiple tracks over one another in sequence. Volume settings.

-handling complex tables of compatible, and incompatible variables. IE, making sure that your fire isn't next to your ice, or that your darkness doesn't go to the same place as your light, or that a given piece of terrain is valid for a given use, etc. the highest prototype code I have running right now, goes up to 36 bools of measurement/comparative data.

-aggregation of global information in an improved and far broader manner. Accrued information can be fed back in 1:1, just like it’s been read and calculated, thus producing feedback-loop driven behavior in any linked game object.

-displaying more intricate text then before, from a larger information pool. Some elements of more in-depth theatrical presentation. hard-wired text data, randomized text data, words strung into sentences, line breaks, and knowing which alignment and origin point text originates from.

-more complex menu design, in order to convey far more complex UI information.

-the modification of design tone, colors and related audio on the fly.

-practice in objects moving from point A to point B at set, modulated speeds. This could include props, characters, or even cameras. As an interesting side discovery, if the rate of movement is set incorrectly it overshoots its target point, constantly jittering around. Useful or annoying? Depends on what your goal is.

-switching cameras, and applying selective visibility settings to objects in conjunction. Key-hold side cameras for special views like “behind the car”, “locked on a target”, “first-person”, etc.
